metaDescription: Legal guide on Irrevocable Power of Attorney for property sale in Bangladesh under Power of Attorney Act 2012. Execution rules, registration fees, and revocation procedure.
keywords: power of attorney land transfer bangladesh
heroIntro: Governed by the Power of Attorney Act 2012 and Power of Attorney Rules 2015, executing an Irrevocable Power of Attorney (Apraptyaharjo Am-Moktarnama) is the principal legal instrument used in real estate development, property sales, and expatriate land management in Bangladesh. Authored by Advocate Md. Shah Alam, Supreme Court Advocate. Call our Uttara chamber at 01712655546.

quickAnswer.heading: ⚡ Key Power of Attorney Essentials
points: Mandatory Registration: Power of attorney involving transfer or sale of immovable property MUST be registered under the Registration Act 1908.
Consular Attestation for Expatriates: NRBs must execute deeds before the Bangladesh Embassy/High Commission abroad.
Irrevocability: Once consideration money is received, the power cannot be unilaterally cancelled without a 30-day registered notice or court decree.

sections.heading: 1. Classification: General vs Irrevocable Power of Attorney
sections.content: Irrevocable powers involving property development or consideration create vested equitable rights in favor of the attorney.

sections.heading: 2. Mandatory Registration & Stamp Duties (2026)
sections.content: Fixed stamp duty and registration fees apply at the Sub-Registry office under government gazette rates.

sections.heading: 3. NRB Consular Attestation from Overseas
sections.content: Deeds executed overseas must be signed before the First Secretary / Consul, attested by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MOFA) Dhaka, and validated by the DC Treasury office.

sections.heading: 4. Limits on Attorney Powers to Sell Land
sections.content: An attorney cannot execute deeds in their own personal name unless specifically authorised in express terms.

sections.heading: 5. Revocation Procedure under Section 13 of 2012 Act
sections.content: To revoke a power of attorney, serve a 30-day statutory notice followed by a registered Deed of Revocation. Consult Advocate Md. Shah Alam at 01712655546.

faq.question: Does a power of attorney remain valid after the principal death?
faq.answer: No. A power of attorney automatically terminates upon the demise of either the principal or the attorney.
